paragraph: The nature of a physical quantity is described by its dimensions. All the physical quantities represented by derived units can be expressed in terms of some combination of seven fundamental or base quantities. We shall call these base quantities as the seven dimensions of the physical world, which are denoted with square brackets [ ]. Thus, length has the dimension [L], mass [M], time [T], electric current [A], thermodynamic temperature [K], luminous intensity [cd], and amount of substance [mol]. The dimensions of a physical quantity are the powers (or exponents) to which the base quantities are raised to represent that quantity. Note that using the square brackets [ ] round a quantity means that we are dealing with ‘the dimensions of’ the quantity.
explanation: Okay soimagine you're building a video game character and you need to describe what each stat means. We call the seven basic building blocks length, mass, time, electric current, temperature, light intensity, and amount of substance, and each one is like an ingredient in a recipe. The dimensions of any physical quantity are just the amounts of each ingredient we use, written as powers, and the square brackets just tell us we're talking about the recipe, not the actual number.

paragraph: In mechanics, all the physical quantities can be written in terms of the dimensions [L], [M] and [T]. For example, the volume occupied by an object is expressed as the product of length, breadth and height, or three lengths. Hence the dimensions of volume are [L] × [L] × [L] = [L]3 = [L3]. As the volume is independent of mass and time, it is said to possess zero dimension in mass [M°], zero dimension in time [T°] and three dimensions in length.
explanation: Think of a cube-shaped box where each side is a length, so the volume is like stacking three lengths together. Since the box doesn't care about how heavy it is or how long it takes to fill, mass and time show up with zero amount, meaning they're raised to the power of zero. So the volume is basically three lengths multiplied, giving L cubed, while mass and time have no part in it.

paragraph:
Similarly, force, as the product of mass and acceleration, can be expressed as
Force = mass × acceleration = mass × (length)/(time)2
The dimensions of force are [M] [L]/[T]2 = [M L T–2]. Thus, the force has one dimension in mass, one dimension in length, and –2 dimensions in time. The dimensions in all other base quantities are zero.
explanation: Picture a heavy shopping cart where the force you need to push it comes from the cart's mass and how quickly you speed it up. The mass gives one dimension, the length part of the acceleration gives another, and the time part is like dividing by time squared, which we say as T to the minus two. All the other ingredients like electric current or temperature don't show up, so they're zero.

paragraph: Note that in this type of representation, the magnitudes are not considered. It is the quality of the type of the physical quantity that enters. Thus, a change in velocity, initial velocity, average velocity, final velocity, and speed are all equivalent in this context. Since all these quantities can be expressed as length/time, their dimensions are [L]/[T] or [L T–1].
explanation: Now here's the cool part: whether you talk about initial velocity, average speed, or final speed, they all share the same kind of dimension because they're all just distance divided by time. It's like different songs in a playlist that all have the same beat tempo, only the actual tempo number changes. So in this view we only care about the type of quantity, not how big or small the number is.
